question:
**Consider the following statements regarding political rivalries in early medieval India:**

**Statement I:** The Rashtrakutas launched several campaigns to gain control over the region of Kanauj.

**Statement II:** The Pratiharas were primarily based in eastern India, while the Palas were established in the western and central regions.

Which of the statements given above is/are **correct**?

options.text: Both Statement I and II are correct
Neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct

solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement I is correct**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
 

• **Statement I:** The **Rashtrakutas** indeed launched several campaigns to gain control over the region of **Kanauj**. 
 
 
• This region was a crucial center of power during the early medieval period (8th to 12th century CE) and was often referred to as the "Kanauj Triangle." 
 
• The Rashtrakutas, Pratiharas, and Palas competed intensely for control over Kanauj due to its strategic location and economic significance. 
 
• The Rashtrakutas, under rulers such as **Dhruva Dharavarsha** and **Govinda III**, launched campaigns against the Pratiharas and Palas to assert dominance over Kanauj. **Hence, Statement I is correct.** 
 
 

• **Statement II:** The geographical distribution of the Pratiharas and Palas mentioned in this statement is incorrect.
